ready2_open_rewrite.final_cot: Image description: The figure is triangle RST. There is a right angle mark at point S, indicating ∠S = 90°. Segment ST is a horizontal side, labeled 5 cm. RT is the hypotenuse, and it is extended outward from point T in the direction of RT; the extension line and the outside of ST form an exterior angle labeled 135°. Reasoning: The interior angle ∠RTS at point T and the marked 135° exterior angle are supplementary, so ∠RTS = 180° - 135° = 45°. The sum of the interior angles of a triangle is 180°, and ∠S = 90°, therefore ∠R = 180° - 90° - 45° = 45°. So △RST is a 45°-45°-90° right triangle; the two legs are equal, and the hypotenuse is √2 times a leg. Since ST = 5 cm, RT = 5√2 cm.
